findings.checklist_item: Select ONE AC5 integration mechanism (merge-onto-prior-snapshot vs confined non-absence path) and specify the exact fetcher/differ data-flow point where the incremental result enters.
evidence: AC5: 'Either the delta is merged onto the prior snapshot before use, or incremental output is confined to a path that never infers deletion.'
fetcher.py:486 '_build_snapshot ... build the normalized snapshot dict' — the snapshot is a COMPLETE picture the differ treats as authoritative (fetcher.py:513-515)
Choosing between the two branches determines blast radius and testability; leaving it open under-specifies the mechanism
findings.finding: AC5 offers two structurally-different integration mechanisms as an unresolved OR ('the delta is merged onto the prior snapshot before use, OR incremental output is confined to a path that never infers deletion'), leaving the actual data-flow undecided. The two differ sharply in blast radius: a merge path touches _build_snapshot/fetch_snapshot's authoritative-snapshot contract (fetcher.py:482-517, consumed by the differ as complete), while a confined path adds a parallel consumer. The plan should commit to one and state where in the fetcher/differ data-flow the incremental result actually enters.
scenarios: Implementer picks the merge branch and must alter the authoritative-snapshot contract shared by fetch_snapshot/compute_snapshot
Implementer picks the confined branch and no existing consumer reads the incremental result, so the capability is wired but dead

findings.checklist_item: Qualify AC10's equivalence claim to the entity classes/window where incremental is actually lossless (e.g. non-deletion, indexing-window-cleared updates), consistent with the plan's stated blind spots.
evidence: AC10: 'returns the same reconciliation decisions as a full-scan pass over the same window'
Plan §'The correctness hazard' and §'The capability is real': 'no tracker's incremental query can report deletions'; JRACLOUD-66284 'the issue does NOT appear in an updated-filtered search'
A same-decisions assertion contradicts the documented blind spots
findings.finding: AC10 requires a measured equivalence ('a pass using incremental fetch returns the same reconciliation decisions as a full-scan pass over the same window'), but the plan itself establishes that incremental CANNOT be equivalent in general: it misses deletions, may miss sub-entity mutations (JRACLOUD-66284 remote-link add/remove), and may miss writes still inside the indexing window. As stated, the acceptance measurement is either unsatisfiable or must be qualified to a window/entity class where equivalence is actually guaranteed.
scenarios: A remote-link removal or a delete occurs in the window: the incremental pass yields a different decision set than the full scan, failing AC10 as literally written

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the watermark's lifecycle: who persists it and where, how it is read on the next pass, its initial value on first run, and its ownership under concurrent/retried passes.
evidence: AC4: 'The capability returns the watermark to resume from, with a documented per-adapter overlap margin'
§2: 'the safe next watermark is not derivable by the caller from the rows alone'
ABSENCE: no plan text names a store, owner, or initialization for the returned watermark
findings.finding: AC4 says the capability 'returns the watermark to resume from', which is stateful across reconciliation passes, but the plan does not specify the watermark's lifecycle: who persists it, where it is stored, how it is read back on the next pass, and how it is initialized/retired. The resume point is shared state whose CREATE/UPDATE/CONSUME/RETIRE path is undefined.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria AC4 and 'return type must carry the next watermark' (§2)
scenarios: First-ever incremental pass has no prior watermark and its initialization is unspecified
Concurrent or retried passes read/write the watermark with no defined ownership

evidence: AC#1: 'search_incremental is implemented on BOTH Jira providers: adapters/jira/ (Cloud) and adapters/jira_datacenter/'
AC#7: 'test_backends_without_incremental_are_detected still passes (FakeBackend stays the negative case)'

A grep for SupportsIncremental surfaces tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_datacenter_backend_port.py:89 `assert not isinstance(_backend(), SupportsIncremental)`; the plan enumerates only the FakeBackend negative test (test_backends_without_incremental_are_detected) in AC#7.
scenarios: tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_datacenter_backend_port.py:89 — test_dc_backend_is_deliberately_not_incremental will FAIL once DC implements search_incremental, since it asserts the DC backend is NOT SupportsIncremental; the plan does not name this test as needing update.

tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_jira_datacenter_backend_port.py:35 — the `SupportsIncremental` import in this test file is a reference the rename branch (SupportsUpdatedSinceFilter) would leave dangling if not enumerated.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC or Scope item: update/replace test_dc_backend_is_deliberately_not_incremental to assert DC now satisfies the capability (matching AC#1), and inventory the imports at test_jira_datacenter_backend_port.py:35, test_backend_capability.py:16/35, and the module-docstring mention at _backend.py:19 if the rename is taken.

findings.checklist_item: Specify that the AC10 equivalence measurement exercises the incremental path against a real or recorded Jira boundary that reproduces index-lag / second-truncation, not an offline stub with an idealized index.
evidence: Plan quote: 'Measured: a pass using incremental fetch returns the same reconciliation decisions as a full-scan pass over the same window'

Plan's own hazard section: 'Atlassian documents the search index lagging writes by "a few seconds to minutes"' and 'Search truncates `updated` to whole seconds' and 'JRACLOUD-66284 ... the issue does NOT appear in an `updated`-filtered search'

Absence rationale: AC does not state the equivalence pass runs against a live or recorded-cassette Jira exhibiting index lag; a fake adapter with an eventually-consistent-free index would bypass the exact defect class the plan flags.
findings.finding: AC10's equivalence measurement ('a pass using incremental fetch returns the same reconciliation decisions as a full-scan pass') does not specify whether it exercises a real/recorded Jira boundary or an offline stub. The very hazards the plan identifies — search-index lag, second-truncation of `updated`, JRACLOUD-66284 remote-link invisibility — are live-boundary phenomena. An offline-only equivalence test that models a clean index would pass green while the production incremental path silently drops writes still inside the indexing window.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, final bullet ('Measured: a pass using incremental fetch returns the same reconciliation decisions...')
findings.suggested_fix: State AC10 as a live-or-cassette test whose fixture includes a write inside the indexing window and a remote-link-only change, asserting the overlap-margin watermark still yields the same decisions as full scan.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide the canonical capability/method name (keep `SupportsIncremental`/`search_incremental` OR commit to `SupportsUpdatedSinceFilter`) and make all ACs and the docstring use it consistently.
evidence: §3: 'The name over-promises... consider `SupportsUpdatedSinceFilter`'
AC1: 'search_incremental is implemented on BOTH Jira providers'
AC2: 'isinstance(backend, SupportsIncremental)' guard
AC7: 'test_backends_without_incremental_are_detected still passes'
findings.finding: Section 3 proposes renaming the capability to `SupportsUpdatedSinceFilter` and the method away from `search_incremental` ('consider'), but every acceptance criterion still uses `SupportsIncremental`/`search_incremental`. The plan neither commits to the rename nor rejects it, leaving the executor to choose the canonical name.
findings.location: Signature defects §3 vs Acceptance Criteria (AC1, AC2, AC7)
scenarios: Executor implements under the old name; a later reader expects the renamed symbol per §3
Round-trip and detection tests reference inconsistent symbol names
findings.suggested_fix: State the chosen name explicitly and update AC1, AC2, AC7, and AC8 to reference the same symbol; if renaming, add an AC covering the rename of the Protocol.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that an incremental-fetch error (timeout/5xx) degrades to the retained full scan, and add a criterion or note surfacing the error rather than swallowing it.
evidence: AC6: 'The periodic full scan is retained and its cadence documented; incremental never replaces it'
AC2: 'Core dispatches through an isinstance guard with a full-scan fallback'
ABSENCE: 'full-scan fallback' is stated only for the isinstance-negative case, not for an incremental call that throws/times out
findings.finding: Incremental is an external Jira search call (a new/altered failure point), but the plan does not state that an incremental-fetch failure degrades to the retained full scan. AC6 retains the full scan as a standing cadence, yet no criterion says incremental errors fall back rather than blocking the pass.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria AC6 and dispatch guard AC2
scenarios: Jira search index errors or times out mid-incremental pass

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Record whether Jira's platform-native `reconcileIssues` parameter (Search and Reconcile doc, same /search/jql endpoint the adapter already POSTs to) is used or explicitly rejected for the read-after-write hazard, and justify the hand-rolled overlap margin against it.
evidence: Atlassian 'Search and Reconcile' (developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/search-and-reconcile/): 'without the reconcileIssues parameter may return stale or outdated data ... If you need read-after-write consistency, you can utilize the reconcileIssues parameter' — this is the same doc the plan cites for the index-lag claim (_backend.py:267 rationale).

Codebase already POSTs to /rest/api/3/search/jql (acli_graph.py:260,299) building request bodies {jql, maxResults, fields} — with NO reconcileIssues field, so the platform mechanism is currently unused.

The plan's overlap-margin design is presented as the only mitigation, with no note weighing it against reconcileIssues (which is partial-fit: it takes explicit issue IDs, so the margin may still be needed — but that trade-off is unstated).
findings.finding: The plan solves Jira's search-index lag / second-truncation with a hand-rolled per-adapter 'overlap margin', but does not consider the platform-native `reconcileIssues` parameter — documented on the exact Atlassian 'Search and Reconcile' page the plan cites, on the same /rest/api/3/search/jql endpoint the codebase already POSTs to — as prior art for read-after-write consistency.
findings.location: Plan §'The correctness hazard' and AC bullet 4 ('a documented per-adapter overlap margin covering Jira's second-truncation and index lag')
scenarios: An incremental pass reads a stale updated watermark because the write is still inside the indexing window; the hand-rolled margin over- or under-corrects where reconcileIssues would have forced consistency for known-changed keys.
A future maintainer re-derives the reconcileIssues option from scratch, unaware the plan already touched the exact endpoint that supports it.
findings.suggested_fix: In the correctness-hazard section, add a paragraph evaluating `reconcileIssues`: note it forces read-after-write consistency only for explicitly-enumerated issue IDs (not open updated-since queries), so it complements rather than replaces the overlap margin — then state the chosen combination (e.g. margin for the general delta, reconcileIssues for keys the reconciler just mutated).
